findings.issue: The lifecycle-mode list names only `new`, `resume` and `restart`, omitting `completed-continue`, the mode `--extend=N` writes on a completed run. The workflow's `lineage_mode` input accepts `auto|resume|restart|completed-continue` (deep-review.yaml:58-59) and `step_extend_completed_run` writes `lineageMode: completed-continue` with `continuedFromRun` (deep-review.yaml:571-572). README.md:141, quick-reference.md:108 and state-format.md:139 all list the fourth mode, so SKILL.md is the stale list.

evidence.out:
58:  lineage_mode: "[auto|resume|restart|completed-continue] - Session lifecycle intent. Default: auto. ... `completed-continue` (from --extend=N: a completed run extended in place by N iterations, same sessionId and generation). `fork` is not accepted. ..."
59:  extend: "[EXTEND] - Positive integer N from --extend=N. Sets lineage_mode to completed-continue and adds N iterations to a completed run. Default: unset."

fix.new: - **Lifecycle modes:** `new`, `resume`, `restart`, and `completed-continue` (set by `--extend=N` on a completed run).

findings.issue: The Decision Priority section says "Checks are evaluated in this order (first match wins)" but its six-item list omits the two checks this topic adds: the `minIterations` floor, which `buildStopDecision` runs after a stop candidate (convergence.cjs:1180-1182), and the `frontierOpen` veto, which runs after the floor and before the legal-stop gates (convergence.cjs:1192-1197). The list also places the clean/composite candidate (item 2) before stuck detection, while the code checks the cap, consecutive failures, stuck, convergence mode and stop policy (convergence.cjs:1136-1161) before selecting a candidate at 1163. Following the documented order does not predict when an open frontier node or the floor holds a stop.

evidence.cmd: rg -n "iterationCount >= maxIterations|consecutiveFailureCount >= CONSECUTIVE_FAILURE_LIMIT|stuckCount >= stuckThreshold|config.convergenceMode === 'off'|config.stopPolicy === 'max-iterations'|let candidate = null|minIterations > 1|config.depthMode === 'expansive'|const evaluated = gatesAt" .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/convergence.cjs

findings.issue: The tuning row tells the operator to pass `--dimensions security,correctness`, but `/deep:review` has no `--dimensions` flag. Its Workflow Flag Surface table (review.md:91-108) lists no dimension flag, and the setup binds `review_dimensions` from Q_dims, the marker, or the default "all" (deep-review-presentation.txt:71, 231); the benchmark scenarios use `--dims`. The `--dimensions` token occurs only in this row across the command and skill trees, so the documented adjustment either is ignored or fails and does not narrow the reviewed dimensions.

The list of checks the frontier veto never outranks omits consecutive failures. `buildStopDecision` returns `STOP` with stop reason `error` once `consecutiveFailureCount` reaches the limit of 3 (convergence.cjs:1147-1148), before the expansive veto at 1192, so a run with three trailing failed iterations stops even while frontier nodes are open. SKILL.md:242, quick-reference.md:165, convergence.md:107 and loop-protocol.md:467 all include consecutive failures in the same list, which makes README.md the outlier.

The packet inventory says the loop uses 9 state files and lists them, but an expansive run also writes `{artifact_dir}/frontier-nodes.jsonl` (frontier-admit.cjs:42, used by seed/admit/close) and reads it back into `registry.frontier` (reduce-state.cjs:2888). The same document documents that store in its "Frontier Node Store (expansive depth only)" section, so the count and table are stale for the mode the section covers.

The config field reference says `continuedFromRun` is set on `resume` and `restart`, but the only non-null writer is `step_extend_completed_run`, which sets it with `lineageMode: completed-continue` (deep-review.yaml:571-572). A restart builds a fresh config with `continuedFromRun: null` (deep-review.yaml:861), and a resume leaves the existing value in place rather than writing it. The description omits `completed-continue`, the mode that actually sets the field.
